spec.name: Sidi Madloum Square
spec.description: Sidi Madloum Square is a historic public space in Ksar el-Kebir named after the Sufi saint Sidi Abdullah al-Madloum. Historically, this area served as the 'Cemetery of the Martyrs of the Battle of Al-Anssora' (1913), where local mujahidin who fought against the Spanish protectorate forces were buried. Today, the square is a vibrant social hub that bridges the city's spiritual heritage with its history of national resistance.

timeline.title: Battle of Al-Anssora
timeline.description: The Battle of Al-Anssora takes place between local tribes and the Spanish army; the site becomes a cemetery for the fallen.

timeline.title: Urban Transformation
timeline.description: The site is transformed from a cemetery into a public square during the city's urban expansion.

comments: The square retains deep symbolic value for its association with the struggle for independence.
